summary: Iter 121 BUG FIX verified: POST /api/tournaments now correctly fires the M&C 'submit' transition, landing tournaments in mc_status=PendingReview with 1 audit chain entry (action=submit, actor=cao-mpca). The backfilled 'Madhavrao Scindia Trophy' is visible in PendingReview to the Hon. Secretary. Secretary can approve via /api/mc/tournament_create/{tid}/transition, flipping the tournament to Approved with a 2-entry chain (submit + approve). CAO cannot self-approve (two-person rule fires with 403). All 14 backend tests pass across the iter121 bug-fix suite (8 tests) + refreshed legacy M&C engine suite (6 tests).

minor.issue: Payload enum values for 'scope' and 'tournament_type' use underscores ('Inter_Divisional', 'MPCA_InterDivisional') not the space-separated forms in the review_request spec ('Inter Divisional', 'mpca_inter_divisional'). Tests were updated to use canonical enum values; consider aliasing or documenting these enums for FE/API consumers.

action_items: None blocking. Optional: expose enum aliases so FE/API callers can send human-friendly values like 'Inter Divisional' with a space.
Optional: emit an audit_log entry when the inline apply_transition raises (currently silently logged via logger.warning) so ops can detect misconfigured workflows.
critical_code_review_comments: tournaments.py L440-444 · The try/except around apply_transition swallows ALL exceptions with just a logger.warning. If the M&C workflow is misconfigured for even one tournament creation, the tournament is silently created without any M&C audit and the user has no signal. Consider bubbling a 202 warning header or persisting the failure into the tournament doc (e.g. mc_status='UnwiredError').
tournaments.py L417 · Redundant ternary `status='Draft' if acceptance.status == 'Pending' else 'Draft'` — always evaluates to 'Draft'. Cosmetic but worth cleaning.

context_for_next_testing_agent: The M&C engine now fires on tournament CREATE. Legacy test_mc_engine.py was refreshed to current roster. If mc_status is missing on an OLD tournament (created before iter121) that's expected — only new tournaments have mc_status populated. All 4 existing tournaments in the DB currently: Ranji Trophy·Plate (Approved), JS Anand Trophy (Approved), AW Kanmadikar Trophy (Draft), Madhavrao Scindia Trophy (PendingReview backfilled). The tournament_create workflow uses body_scope=State + post_title='Chief Accounts Officer' (maker) and 'Hon. Secretary' (checker) with requires_two_person=true on approve+reject.
rca of the issue: Root cause: POST /api/tournaments (routes/tournaments.py L324) inserted directly into MongoDB without invoking lib.mc.apply_transition, so no mc_status/mc_chain/mc_approvals were ever set and the tournament never appeared in Hon. Secretary's approval inbox. Fix applied in code: (a) inject Request param on the endpoint; (b) initialise doc['mc_status']='Draft', mc_chain=[], mc_approvals=[] before insert; (c) after insert, call apply_transition(wf_key='tournament_create', doc_id=t.id, action='submit', principal=get_principal(request), note=None) inside try/except so a mis-configured workflow doesn't lose the tournament. Verified E2E: create as CAO returns mc_status=PendingReview and 1 chain entry (actor_id='cao-mpca', action='submit'). Two-person rule verified: CAO gets 403 attempting to approve their own submission; Secretary approves and doc.mc_status flips to 'Approved' with 2 chain entries.
